Announcements.FullBody:
Applications for Mini-Grants from our Profs for a Purpose: Suicide Prevention Walk are now open!  The annual Rowan Profs for a Purpose: Suicide Prevention Walk is an event each April or May that allows our campus community to honor lives lost to suicide and also educate and support our community on suicide prevention and mental health. We also provide resources and share in activities that ignite hope and care. Participation is free, but individuals and teams can also donate to this cause. Every dollar donated directly supports Rowan students, faculty, staff and community through supportive and educational programming and efforts for suicide prevention and improving mental health. Last year our walk raised over $5,000! All of those funds raised at the Profs for a Purpose: Suicide Prevention Walk were raised by individuals and their commitment to mental health and suicide prevention - this speaks volumes for how much our community cares! One of the ways those funds are distributed is through our Mini-Grants. 

This year we are awarding up to $3,000 in grants named in honor of the top 5 teams from 2026 in order of funds raised: Mental Health Warriors, Thriving Together, RLUH & Friends, Social Work in Action, Rowan Catholic Campus Ministry. Students, Faculty, Staff and other Rowan community members are all eligible to apply for a grant for up to $300. The grant recipients may include a list of items for purchase, and those items will be processed through the Center for Well-Being office, or the grant recipient may choose to receive the grant via DCA. Grants can only be dispersed in these two ways.  

Projects should support efforts to address mental health, mental illness, or suicide prevention through one or more of the following: education, resources, belonging/connection, and/or research. Mini grants will be awarded for projects that will take place before September 2027. Application Deadline is Friday, October 23rd, 2026 by 4pm and recipients will be announced on Wednesday, November 4th, 2026. Please note: anyone who was awarded a mini-grant in the fall of 2025 will be eligible to apply again in fall of 2027 (i.e. If you’re a recipient of a previous grant, you must wait one year to reapply).

Application can be found at this link: https://forms.gle/kfYnZPkJFkN4D4bB8 or you can find more information here: https://go.rowan.edu/ProfsMiniGrant

And Join us for our 10th Profs for A Purpose: Suicide Prevention Walk taking place Saturday, April 17th,  2027.

At Rowan, our strength lies in bringing different voices together. We are committed to building a campus culture where everyone feels truly seen, heard, and valued.

We invite you to the You Belong Summit 2026: Learn It. Practice It. Live It. This summit launches the new Belonging Series and Certification, a professional development initiative that supports Rowan University's commitment to ensuring everyone is seen, heard, and valued. Join us to hear powerful stories, learn about the Belonging Series and Professional Learning Community, and be part of creating a more connected campus.

Summit Highlights:

  • When: November 19, 2026 (choose a morning or afternoon session).
  • What: Real stories, belonging strategies, and a space to commit to a more connected campus.
  • Next Steps: Get a first look at our five-module Belonging Certification and register for the spring cohort on-site.

Mark your calendars and register today!

  https://forms.gle/iR7gs1GWi53d2VeP7

 

We look forward to seeing you there.

Division of Student Access and Pathway Programs

  • AI Literacy Course Pack

  • Support

Directions to get started can be found on the Hypothesis at Rowan webpage.

Academic Integrity: Resources and Reminders for Faculty 

As the Fall term nears, we encourage faculty to consider how you can build a culture of trust and respect in your courses as a foundation for academic integrity.

Rowan has many resources available to help faculty learn more about academic integrity. These resources can help you understand why students might commit academic integrity violations and offer strategies to engage students in their own learning, decreasing the likelihood of violations. 

  • Rowan University’s Academic Integrity Website – Provides videos and FAQs for both students and faculty members about academic integrity and the processes at Rowan University.
  • Canvas Commons Academic Integrity Module – This Canvas module contains helpful information about academic integrity resources at Rowan and can be imported directly into your course shells. It can be accessed through a search for “academic integrity” in Canvas Commons. 
  • Faculty Handbook on Academic Integrity  – This Canvas course allows faculty to explore as much (or as little) as desired about academic integrity. Faculty can either engage with resources directly in the modules, or browse a more structured course experience. Topics include an overview of academic integrity, proactive strategies for encouraging academic integrity, and details of the academic integrity violation process at Rowan. To request access  you can email academicintegrity@rowan.edu.
    • Once  you have been added to the course, you will receive notification through your Rowan e-mail and/or a pop-up that will appear the next time Canvas is opened.  Once the course invitation is accepted, faculty will be able to browse the handbook and access it whenever needed. 
       

Generative AI. Under Rowan’s Academic Integrity Policy, faculty may elect to prohibit the use of generative artificial intelligence in their classroom and should clearly outline their expectations in their syllabus. Faculty should report academic integrity violations (AIV) involving the use of artificial intelligence. Please note the Provost’s Office does not accept reports from “artificial intelligence detectors” as evidence of an AIV.  Other evidence (e.g. fabricated citations, discovery interviews formatting consistent with AI, writing comparisons) may be included in a report as evidence of an academic integrity violation. More information can be found in the above-mentioned resources.

Turnitin. The Rowan University Turnitin Policy requires that, if faculty wish to use Turnitin in a course,

  1. Faculty MUST include a statement regarding the use and purpose of Turnitin in the official course syllabus
  2. Students have the right to not submit personally identifiable information to Turnitin
  3. Students should be provided either an opt-in or opt-out statement (see policy for suggestions).
  4. Aligned with this policy, the Office of the Provost will not accept Turnitin reports as admissible evidence for a Report of an Academic Integrity Violation unless such statements are included in the course syllabus. 

If faculty have any questions about academic integrity or the academic integrity process at Rowan, please reach out to Tricia Yurak, Provost’s Fellow for Academic Integrity, or Doug Mann, Faculty Fellow for Academic Integrity, by emailing academicintegrity@rowan.edu. Thank you for your efforts to uphold academic integrity in your courses.

The Office of Research Development (ORD) invites internal applications for the 2027 Searle Scholars Program, a prestigious limited submission opportunity supporting exceptional early-career faculty pursuing innovative research in the biomedical sciences.

The Searle Scholars Program recognizes outstanding investigators conducting high-impact research at the intersection of biology, chemistry, medicine, and related disciplines.

Key Dates:

  • Sponsor Deadline: September 30, 2026
  • Rowan Internal Deadline: August 1, 2026, at 5:00 PM (EST)

Award Overview:

  • Award Amount: $450,000 over three years ($150,000 annually)
  • Supports independent research of exceptional early-career faculty.
  • Emphasizes innovative, high-risk, high-reward scientific research.
  • Provides significant national recognition and enhances institutional research prestige.

Eligibility:

Applicants must:

  • Hold a tenure-track appointment at the Assistant Professor level (or the nearest equivalent).
  • Have begun their first appointment as an independent investigator on or after May 1, 2025.
  • Be in their first tenure-track position (or the nearest equivalent).
  • Demonstrate exceptional promise for independent research leadership in the biomedical sciences.

Applicants should carefully review the sponsor's complete eligibility requirements prior to applying.

Limited Submission Guidance:

  • Rowan University is limited in the number of nominations permitted by the sponsor.
  • If the number of internal applicants exceeds the institutional limit, ORD will conduct a competitive internal review to determine the University's nominee(s).

Internal Application Requirements:

Interested faculty should submit:

  • Research Summary (maximum two pages) describing the proposed research vision, significance, and innovation.
  • NIH Biosketch
  • Statement of Eligibility, including the date of the applicant's first independent tenure-track (or equivalent) faculty appointment.

Please submit all materials to ORD@rowan.edu no later than August 1, 2026, at 5:00 PM (EST).

Strategic Positioning:

This opportunity aligns with Rowan University's continued investment in:

  • Translational and biomedical research
  • Early-career faculty excellence
  • National research competitiveness
  • Institutional research prestige

Participation provides an opportunity to advance Rowan's most promising early-career investigators while strengthening the University's national research profile.

Questions:

Faculty interested in applying or discussing their competitiveness are encouraged to contact the Office of Research Development at ORD@rowan.edu.

 

Johnny Manuel

Institutional Nomination Limit: One (1) nominee

The Office of Research Development (ORD) invites eligible Rowan University faculty to participate in the internal limited submission competition for the Brain Research Foundation (BRF) 2027 Seed Grant Program.

BRF’s Seed Grant Program supports new and innovative neuroscience research projects with the potential to generate preliminary data and become competitive for NIH or other external funding. Rowan University may nominate only one faculty member, inclusive of all campuses and medical schools.

Eligibility

Applicants must be:

  • Full-time Assistant or Associate Professors; and
  • Conducting research in neuroscience, neurology, neurobiology, physiology, psychiatry, psychology, or related disciplines; and
  • Proposing a scientific project focused on brain health or disease, including cancer.

Award

The selected nominee may request up to $100,000 in direct costs for a two-year project period, with $50,000 anticipated in each year, subject to BRF requirements.

Internal Submission Requirements

Faculty interested in consideration as Rowan’s institutional nominee should submit:

  • A brief project summary/research plan describing the proposed research, innovation, and significance;
  • A statement describing the project's potential to generate preliminary data and position the investigator for future external funding;
  • A current NIH-style biosketch or CV

Internal applications must be received by Tuesday, October 13, 2026.

Following internal review, one Rowan University nominee will be selected and provided sufficient time to prepare and submit the required BRF Letter of Intent by November 3, 2026.

Faculty are encouraged to begin preparing early. 

Questions regarding the internal competition or limited submission process may be directed to the Office of Research Development (ORD) at ORD@rowan.edu

The Office of Research Development (ORD) is coordinating Rowan University’s internal selection process for the 2027 Andrew Carnegie Fellows Program. Rowan may nominate one tenured and one untenured scholar.

The program is open to academics, journalists, and public intellectuals. Nominees must hold a Ph.D. or other terminal degree or be a high-level professional working outside academia. Proposed research should demonstrate the potential to inform responses to political polarization and offer lessons for addressing harmful polarization or enhancing social cohesion in the United States.

Rowan Internal Deadline: Friday, October 23, 2026
Sponsor Deadline: Friday, November 13, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET

Interested Rowan faculty should submit materials through the Office of Research Development (ORD) limited submission process for consideration. Selected nominees will receive instructions and support for completing the sponsor submission.

PROFessional(s) of the Month is for faculty, staff, or employee groups at any level across all University campuses. The monthly recipient(s), chosen by the Employee Recognition Committee, will receive a special visit by this group of professionals dedicated to recognizing—and celebrating—outstanding work by Rowan employees.

Which Rowan professional or team of professionals has gone beyond the call of duty in serving the University community? Who in the past month exhibited terrific employee and/or student engagement, customer service, and teamwork, exemplifying all that is exceptional about Rowan professionals? 

In short, who should be Rowan’s PROFessional(s) of the Month? 

View past honorees: PROFessionals of the Month 

Nominations can be submitted for individual employees, work groups or project teams. The ideal candidate(s) will have played a major role in a recent, exceptional accomplishment, preferably in or just prior to the month they have been nominated for (Examples: Completion of a high impact task or project, successful organization of an event, receipt of an award for an extraordinary accomplishment, etc.).   

To nominate faculty, staff, or a team of professionals for the PROFessional(s) of the Month, fill out this form by the end of the calendar month to explain why your nominee(s) should be recognized. Feel free to re-submit nominations that were previously submitted!

Life & Liberty: the 26|27 Marie Rader Series Season

Reflecting on America’s 250th with an emphasis on singular African American artists, the Life & Liberty season includes: 

  • Sounds Like America with Lara Downes & Rhiannon Giddens - October 30
  • Dee Dee Bridgewater & Bill Charlap - January 31
  • Rennie Harris Puremovement American Street Dance Theater - February 20 & 21
  • The Snowy Day and Other Stories by Ezra Jack Keats - March 14

ABOUT THE SERIES

The Marie Rader Series brings world-class artists to campus for public performances, masterclasses, visits with community groups and more. With great concessions, free tickets for Rowan students, discounts for Rowan employees and alumni, and accommodations for accessibility, the Marie Rader Series invites YOU to find your next uplifting performing arts experience right here at Rowan! 

Read more about the series here or visit go.rowan.edu/marieraderseries for tickets and information.

For graduate (or higher) level students, the course registration opening date is changing!

Beginning the Spring 2027 course registration cycle, students who are coded at the graduate or higher level will be able to access the registration interface one day prior to the undergraduate open date. This means that, for Spring 2027 course registration, graduate students will be able to register on Monday, October 26. The full registration schedule can be found on this page.

This timeline will be in effect for all Spring and Fall course registration cycles, moving forward. As always, when registering, if students encounter an error (missing prerequisites, closed course, college restriction, etc.), they should contact the course professor or the academic department that houses the course, directly, to request the appropriate registration waiver.

The English Language Program (ELP) at Rowan University is back on our Camden Campus and will maintain classes on our Glassboro Campus starting September 1!

These classes are open to anyone who is a multilingual (ESL) learner and wants to improve their language skills for academic or personal growth. We offer 5 Levels and accept all levels of proficiency!

Glassboro

Schedule:  9 a.m. - 2:35 p.m. Monday - Thursday

Costs:

International Students - $1500 per 7 week-session / $3000 a semester

Local / New Jersey residents - $750 per 7-week session / $1500 per semester 

Camden

Schedule: 10 a.m. - 1 p.m. Monday - Thursday

Costs:

Local / New Jersey residents - $550 per 7-week session / $1100 per semester.

Outside of New Jersey - $1500 per 7-week session / $3000 a semester.

$45.00 application fee is waived using the code: CAMDEN

Online/Hybrid options are available!

If interested, please contact elp@rowan.edu or 856.256.5768 - We are on WhatsApp - Se habla español.
